display.text:
# Context Pack: `sprint-execute-resume` — Sprint execute queue and resume Target: ultraplan-go @ 8eef70f4903b25580719960009a170945bdad9ad (frozen, clean tree). Planning context: ultraplan-workspace @ ab12dc38059c9bf485f9aced9075bcd7d924cac5. Domain: governed-sprint-delivery. Risk: high. Descriptive only — no defect judgments. ## 1. Purpose Executes the top-level task checkboxes of a validated `plan.md` through a reusable agent session, with product-owned durability around every agent turn: - **Queue execution**: one ordered pass over plan tasks; first turn gets shared sprint context + full queue; later turns are compact continuations in the same session when a reusable session ID exists (fallback: independent full prompts). - **Persist-before-launch checkpointing**: each task is persisted as `running` before the runtime call, and its terminal outcome is persisted before the next task starts; session IDs observed mid-stream are also checkpointed. - **Stop-on-failure discipline**: queue halts on the first failed or cancelled task. - **Stale-running reconcile**: `running` records left by dead owners become `failed` with diagnostics at three distinct points (startup recovery, resume reconciliation, pre-execution check). - **Deferral protocol**: CLI `--defer --reason` (operator) or an agent-authored plan marker `- [/] Task N: ... — Deferred: ` (agent); both require rationale and produce durable `deferred` outcomes; the plan checkbox stays visibly unchecked. - **Resume validation**: `--resume` allows checked/deferred plan markers only when the run state already records matching terminal outcomes per stable task ID. - **Containment**: the agent's working directory is set to the resolved approved target (worktree preferred), with in-prompt safety constraints forbidding git mutation and out-of-scope artifacts. - **Publication**: when every task resolves (complete|deferred), git publication commits the implementation worktree (`All=true`) then the workspace artifacts (`execute.md`, `.run-state.json`), config-gated. Primary code: `internal/sprint/execute.go`, `execute_plan.go`, `execute_state.go`, `execute_target.go`, `execute_model.go`, plus `internal/sprint/publication.go:57-78` and `internal/app/git_publication.go`. ## 2. Entrypoints and control flow ### CLI dispatch (`internal/app/sprint_commands.go:329-368`) - Flag parsing `parseSprintExecuteArgs` (1193-1233): `--task `, `--dry-run|--prompt`, `--resume`, `--defer --reason `, `--model `. Constraints: `--defer` requires `--task`; `--defer` cannot combine with `--dry-run`, `--resume`, or `--model`. Unknown flags → ExitUsage. - Non-dry-run, non-defer runs are wrapped as durable operations: `beginDurableCLICommand(OperationExecuteStart, ...Task: req.TaskID)` (durable_operations.go:49-138 — run-control acceptance, owner claim with lease+fencing, running lifecycle event, heartbeat/cancel-watch goroutine). The command context becomes cancellation-aware. Service is rebuilt via `sprintRuntimeService` (685-711) with the real runtime, publisher (`stagePublisher`: nil publisher when `git.stage_completion=off`), stage runtime models, QA/smoke settings. - Deferral runs `DeferExecuteTask` on the plain (non-runtime) service against `deps.ctx`; no durable wrapper. - Error classification after render: findings present → ExitValidation; error contains "failed tasks" → ExitPartial; contains "runtime" → ExitRuntime; otherwise `mapSprintError`. - Output rendering `renderSprintExecute` (1372-1402): project/sprint, dry-run prompt dump, result message, run-state/summary paths, per-task `id status attempts=N` lines, findings list. Help text at 1530-1531, 1571-1580. ### Web / TUI / flow entrypoints - Web operation spec `"execute"|"execute-start"` maps to `OperationExecuteStatus | OperationExecuteDryRun | OperationExecuteResume | OperationExecuteStart` based on options (`internal/web/operation_handlers.go:646-666`). TUI exposes Execute Status/Dry Run/Start/Resume nav items (`internal/tui/model.go:480-483`). - `internal/app/operation_runner.go:53-58`: execute-start/resume → `service.Execute(ctx, p, s, ExecuteRequest{TaskID, ModelOverride, Resume: kind==OperationExecuteResume})`; dry-run variant at `operations.go:443`. - Flow integration (`internal/sprint/flow.go`): execute is the 8th cumulative stage; `runFlowStage` case StageExecute → `s.Execute(ctx, ..., ExecuteRequest{DryRun: req.DryRun, Resume: true})` (flow.go:241) — flow always resumes. Flow skips its generic planning-stage publication for execute (execute publishes itself, flow.go:142-155, 167) and uses `ExecuteComplete` for the skip check (flow.go:307-308 → verify.go:134-140). ### `Service.Execute` main loop (`internal/sprint/execute.go:129-349`) 1. Acquire mutation lock unless DryRun (`acquireMutationContext`, locks.go:112-126 — cross-process file lease shared by flow/execute/review/smoke/verify; reentrant via context marker). 2. `prepareExecute` (351-384): resolve sprint inputs → `planManifest` → `resolveSprintTarget(create=false)` → read plan artifact → `extractExecutePlanTasks(data, manifest, allowChecked=req.Resume)` → if Resume, `validateResolvedResumeTasks` → TaskID existence check → `executeModelSelection(override)` (override > planning.execute_model > planning.plan_model > runtime provider/model; unresolved model ⇒ finding). Any finding aborts before any write ("execute prerequisites failed validation"). 3. Read planning inputs; `prepareSharedPromptContext(..., persistCache=true)` — code-context-derived shared prefix, cached context pack, fails closed when code-context exists but is invalid (`prompt_context.go:93-123`). 4. DryRun: composes the first (or selected) task's prompt and returns; no state writes, no runtime. 5. Fresh vs resumed state: `records := ExecuteTasksToRecords(tasks, now)`; `state := NewExecuteRunState(sp, target, planPath, PlanFingerprint(mustReadPlan), records, now)`. If `req.Resume` AND load succeeds → `state = reconcileExecuteState(existing, records, now)` (existing records substituted by ID into planned order; stale `running` → `failed` with "recovered stale running task on resume"). Load errors on resume are ignored (fresh state wins). Then unconditional `SaveExecuteRunState`. 6. `executionQueue := executeQueueFromState(state.Tasks, tasks, req.TaskID)` — planned tasks whose record is not complete/deferred, optionally narrowed to one ID. 7. Session reuse gate (186-193): only when `req.Resume` and `state.Target.Path == target.Path`; picks the last filtered record whose Runtime.Model equals the first queued task's effective model and has a SessionID (`reusableExecuteSession`, 563-574). 8. Per-task loop over `state.Tasks` (skips others when TaskID set): - Skip `complete`; `running` → `failed` + "stale-running ... before resume" diagnostic; proceed only if now pending|failed|cancelled. - Mark running, `Attempts++`, StartedAt; persist — failure aborts before launch ("persist running execute task %q"). - Per-task model: inline plan annotation `` overrides batch selection (`executeSelectionForTask`, 739-744). - `continueSession := batchSessionID != "" && models match` → compact `RenderExecuteContinuationPrompt` with empty prefix and `SessionAction="continue"`; otherwise full `renderExecuteSessionPrompt` (RenderExecutePrompt + ordered queue section + direct-input packet: project definition inputs, sprint-index, technical-handbook, reasoning directory inputs, reasoning.md, plan.md). - Metadata: session_mode initial|continue|fresh-fallback, execution_turn, execution_queue_size, model_source, stage, task. - `runtimeRequest` (service.go:1122-1169): scoped runtime store owner/path under the sprint dir, PromptRef with sha256 checksum, trace ID, stable-prefix cache directive. `runtimeReq.WorkDir = target.Path` (execute.go:245). `OnEvent` wrapper checkpoints any new SessionID into run state under a mutex (save errors captured, surfaced post-run). - `startSprintRuntime` (runtime_metrics.go:116-125): `pruntime.CleanupRuntimeStores(sp.Path, 72h, 2GiB, false)` then `runtime.StartRun`; runtime metrics persisted separately (failure degrades to warning). - Post-run classification precedence (287-313): checkpoint save error → failed/"state-save-failed"; deferral read-back error → failed/"invalid-deferral"; deferral reason non-empty → deferred + rationale diagnostic; ctx cancelled → cancelled; runtime error → failed/"runtime-failed"; ≥1 artifact → complete + evidence entries (paths sanitized by `safeArtifactPath`); warning containing "diagnostic-only" → complete + "diagnostic-only-completion"; else failed/"missing-evidence". - Terminal state persisted ("persist terminal execute task"); checkpoint errors abort the whole command afterwards. Failed or cancelled breaks the loop; single-task mode always breaks. - On success, batchSessionID/batchSessionModel advance from the run result (or task.Runtime fallback). 9. `WriteExecuteSummary` → `projects/

/sprints//execute.md` (plain `os.WriteFile` 0644 inside contained path): counts per status, per-task attempts/evidence/diagnostics lines. 10. Any failed/cancelled ⇒ returns result plus error "execute completed with failed tasks". 11. Best-effort `_ = s.deleteCompletedSessions(...)` per runtime result (deletes session(s)/runtime store; flow.go:26-56). 12. If `allExecuteTasksResolved` (≥1 task, all complete|deferred) → `publishExecuteStage` (publication.go:57-78): implementation publish `{Root: target.Path, All: true}` then workspace publish of `execute.md` + `.run-state.json`; identical commit message "ultraplan: sprint

/ complete execute" with `UltraPlan-Publication:` identity trailer; skipped results filtered when publisher disabled. ### `DeferExecuteTask` (execute.go:29-79) Trims reason; requires non-empty taskID+reason, ≤1000 chars, no `\x00\r\n`. Mutation lock; loads state; rejects deferring complete/deferred tasks; marks deferred (+CompletedAt, "deferred" diagnostic with redacted reason); saves state and summary; unknown ID errors. Does not modify plan.md. ### Resume validation (`validateResolvedResumeTasks`, execute.go:386-421) When resuming and plan.md has `[x]` or `[/]` top-level markers: requires a loadable valid run state ("checked tasks lack execution state" otherwise); each resolved marker must map to matching status (`[x]`→complete, `[/]`→deferred) by task ID; mismatches become blocking findings. ### Target resolution (`ResolveExecuteTarget` / `resolveSprintTarget`, execute_target.go) - Extract `**Target Implementation Directory:**` (bold or plain bullet, backtick-trimmed) from project-index.md; absolute or workspace-root-relative; must stat to an existing directory. - If `.workspace.json` exists it wins (Source ".workspace.json"): validated against current source root (clean-path equality), worktree dir exists and is a dir, same git common dir as source, current branch equals recorded branch. Invalid → findings; unreadable/malformed → findings; absent + create=false → raw source target. - Worktree creation happens at the code-context stage (`create=true` in flow.go:138), not here: `createSprintWorkspace` requires the source be a clean git worktree root (no uncommitted changes), creates `ultraplan//` branch at HEAD under sibling `.basename-ultraplan-worktrees/` dir, writes `.workspace.json` atomically (rollback removes worktree+branch if the record write fails). ### Publication mechanics (`internal/platform/gitpublish/publisher.go`) Modes off|commit|commit-and-push. Resolves repo root + current branch (detached HEAD rejected), acquires `ultraplan-publish.lock` in the git common dir, builds a temporary index (`read-tree parent`, `add -A -- paths`, `write-tree`), skips commit when tree equals parent tree, else `commit-tree -p parent` + `update-ref commit parent` (CAS against concurrent branch movement) + index reconcile. Push honors upstream remote/ref, else pushes HEAD to configured remote with `--set-upstream`; `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, push timeout (default 2m). Path requests are containment-checked against the repo root. ## 3. Inputs / outputs Inputs: - argv flags; workspace root; cwd/env via workspace discovery. - `project-index.md` `Project Scope > Target Implementation Directory` line (agent-writable planning artifact; selects both the agent workdir and the wholesale-commit root). - `plan.md` content: top-level `- [ ] Task N: Name` checkboxes (bold-tolerant), nested `- [ ]` steps, `>` quote lines scanned for `Decision N` / `REQ-N-N` / `AC-N` refs, evidence heuristics (step text containing evidence/verification/test/check), `- [/]` deferral markers with `— Deferred:`/`- Deferred:` suffix reasons, inline `` annotations. Plan must pass `ValidatePlanContent` against the plan manifest first. - Planning inputs packet (requirements/code-context/sprint-index/handbook/reasoning dirs/reasoning.md/plan.md) rendered into the first-turn prompt. - `.run-state.json` or productstate DB record (schemaVersion 1) for resume/status; legacy schemaVersion-0 terminal files recognized read-only. - `.workspace.json` worktree record; config keys (`planning.execute_model`, `planning.plan_model`, `models.primary/default`, `git.stage_completion|remote|push_timeout`, runtime config); live agent runtime. Outputs: - Human stdout render; exit codes (0 ok / 2 usage / validation-class / partial for failed tasks / runtime-class). - Files written: `.run-state.json` (atomic temp+fsync+rename+dir-sync, JSON indent+newline), `execute.md` (plain truncate-write), runtime metrics file, disposable context-pack cache. - Git commits and optional pushes in two repos (implementation worktree, workspace) when all tasks resolved and publishing enabled. - Durable run-control events (accept/claim/lifecycle/heartbeat/terminal) for non-dry-run CLI executions. - Runtime side effects delegated to the agent: file edits inside WorkDir=target.Path, test execution, etc. ## 4. Authoritative state - **`.run-state.json` schemaVersion 1** (`domain.go:12,122-133`): header {schemaVersion, project, sprint, target{path,source}, planPath (contained relative), planFingerprint `sha256:` of whitespace-normalized lowercase plan text, createdAt, updatedAt} + ordered `tasks[]` {id `task-<12 hex>`, identity{name, planLine≥1, decisions[], requirements[], evidence[]}, status, attempts≥0, createdAt, updatedAt, startedAt?, completedAt?, diagnostics[], evidence[], runtime?}. - Statuses: pending / running / complete / deferred / failed / cancelled; terminal = complete|deferred|failed|cancelled (`domain.go:63-70`, execute_state.go:271-273). - **Validation contract** `ValidateExecuteRunState` (execute_state.go:184-268): strict schemaVersion==1; project/sprint identity match; safe contained planPath; fingerprint charset (no `\x00\r\n`); ≥1 task; unique IDs; safe identity text; deferred requires completedAt + a `deferred` diagnostic with non-blank rationale; running requires startedAt; terminal requires completedAt; diagnostics need code+message+time and safe charset; evidence needs kind+summary and optionally a safe relative path. - **Dual-home behavior**: when the productstate DB is enabled, the DB record is authoritative — `Save` writes DB first, then mirrors the file only once every task is terminal (checkpoint semantics, execute_state.go:105-130); `Load` prefers the DB record (state_database.go:38-55). Otherwise the file is primary. Migration hooks exist (`MigrateExecuteStateToDatabase`). - **Legacy compatibility**: schemaVersion-0 `{status: complete|failed|cancelled, files[], testsRun[], blockers[]}` files are historical evidence only (`LegacyTerminalExecuteStatus`), never resumable; `requireCompleteExecute` (verify.go:100-132) additionally accepts that legacy shape (status complete/completed with files[] plus non-empty execute.md) as completion evidence. - **`.workspace.json`** (`execute_target.go:16-27`): {schemaVersion:1, sourceRoot, path, branch, baseline, createdAt}; created at code-context stage; validated on every execute target resolution. - **`execute.md`**: derived human summary; plain WriteFile (not atomic); regenerated after every run/deferral. - **`plan.md`**: user-owned input; execute never writes it. The *agent* may edit markers during a turn; execute re-reads it after each turn (`agentDeferredTaskReason`, 423-450: full manifest + extraction revalidation, returning the marker reason only for the exact task). The recorded `PlanFingerprint` is captured once at state creation (via `mustReadPlan`, which swallows read errors) and is not re-verified later in the loop. - Note (descriptive): a resume attempt with unchecked plan tasks but an unreadable/malformed `.run-state.json` passes prepareExecute (no resolved markers ⇒ no findings; load error ignored at execute.go:177) and proceeds with fresh state, overwriting the prior file on first save. ## 5. Invariants (as implemented) - No runtime launch before the `running` transition is durably saved; no queue advance before the terminal outcome is saved; mid-stream session-ID events are also checkpointed. - Queue stops at the first failed or cancelled task; completed/deferred tasks are never re-executed within a run. - Resume reconciliation matches strictly by deterministic ID (normalized name+decisions+requirements+evidence hash); renamed/edited tasks get new IDs and their old records drop out of the reconciled list; deferral markers and model annotations deliberately do not change IDs (test-asserted). - Stale-running recovery exists in three layers: `ReconcileInterruptedMutation` (startup, code "recovery-interrupted"), `reconcileExecuteState` (resume), and the in-loop pre-execution check ("before resume"). - Deferral requires rationale at every layer: CLI flag validation, plan-marker regex requiring a reason, state-validation rationale diagnostic, and `invalid-deferral` classification when the read-back fails. - Completion gating: success requires ≥1 runtime artifact or an explicit "diagnostic-only" warning; otherwise failed/"missing-evidence". - Agent workdir is exactly the resolved target path (worktree preferred when valid); evidence paths stored in state must be safe relative paths or dropped. - Publication happens only when all tasks are terminal-resolved (complete|deferred); implementation repo commits before workspace artifacts; both silently skipped when publishing is off. - All persisted messages/diagnostics route through redaction/truncation helpers (`safeExecuteText` → `config.RedactValue`, ≤180 chars via `safeError`). - Session reuse additionally requires unchanged target path and equal effective model; otherwise fresh full prompts ("fresh-fallback"). ## 6. Trust boundaries - **plan.md as control input**: checkbox syntax, task names, decision/requirement references, deferral reasons, and `` annotations are parsed from an agent-writable artifact. The annotation string flows into runtime model selection without charset restriction beyond the annotation regex `[A-Za-z0-9._~/-]+`; marker deferral reasons are captured by regex without length limits at parse time (charset-checked later at state validation; redacted at persistence). - **project-index.md** decides which directory the agent may mutate and which repository gets committed wholesale (`All=true`) at publication. - **Agent output → durable state**: artifacts/warnings/session IDs from the runtime become state records; evidence URI must pass `safeRelPath` else stored empty; all free-text redacted. - **Agent constraints are prompt-level** (`ExecuteSafetyInstructions`, execute_target.go:220-227): stay inside approved target; do not create smoke/review/issues artifacts; do not run/request git mutation; no cross-sprint/TUI/hosted work. Technical enforcement of sandbox/permissions belongs to the opencode-agent-runtime surface (configured sandbox/permission policy travels on the runtime request). - **gitpublish** executes git with sanitized env (`GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, LC_ALL=C), validates remote names (no leading dash, restricted charset), and CAS-updates the branch ref. - **Mutation serialization**: cross-process sprint mutation lease (file lock) plus durable run-control owner fencing serialize execute against flow/review/smoke/verify and other owners. ## 7. External effects & lifecycle semantics - Mutates the implementation repo (through the delegated agent), can commit and push it, commits workspace artifacts, deletes completed sessions/runtime stores best-effort, prunes stale runtime stores (>72h, >2GiB). - **Cancellation**: durable-context cancel during a turn classifies the task cancelled (+diagnostic), breaks the queue, persists, returns result with error; run-control finish records cancelled. The in-flight runtime call receives the same ctx. - **Crash/restart**: orphaned `running` records recover to failed on startup reconcile or next resume; cleanup-uncertain marker forces explicit operator handling instead of silent reconcile (locks.go:40-44,101-108); legacy terminal states remain readable. - **Retry**: rerunning without `--resume` rebuilds fresh state (prior file replaced on first save); failed/cancelled/pending tasks restart with Attempts++; `--resume` keeps complete/deferred history and continues the remaining queue, reusing the session when target and model still match. - **Partial failure**: mixed-status state persisted, execute.md reflects counts, command exits ExitPartial-class with "execute completed with failed tasks". - Publication failure after full resolution surfaces as command error while leaving all tasks resolved and state saved (commit may exist without push; push timeout bounded). ## 8. Immediate surface dependencies - **sprint-planning-chain**: `resolveSprintInputs`, `planManifest`, `ValidatePlanContent`, plan artifact reads, direct-input packet composition, shared prompt prefix/context pack. - **sprint-flow-state**: flow dispatches execute (always Resume:true), skips its own publish step for execute, gates skip-checks via `ExecuteComplete`; execute itself does not write flow-state.json. - **opencode-agent-runtime** (`internal/platform/runtime`): Request/Result/Event contract — SessionID/SessionAction continuation, OnEvent stream, Artifacts/Warnings driving completion classification, RuntimeStore scoping/cleanup, usage/metrics summaries. - **repo-publication** (`internal/platform/gitpublish`): policy modes, repo lock, temp-index commit strategy, push semantics. - **product-state-mirror** (`internal/productstate`): authoritative DB record {header, items keyed by task ID with ordinals} behind `ExecuteStateInDatabase`. - **run-control / durable operations**: acceptance, claim, fencing, heartbeats, cancellation watch, terminal proposals wrapping every non-dry-run CLI execute. - **workspace scaffold**: embedded `prompts/execute-sprint.md` documents the superseded agent-authored execution mode (writes legacy schemaVersion-0-style `.run-state.json` itself); still materialisable via `defaults install`. ## 9. Contracts (CURRENT-CONTRACT evidence) From target-repo `docs/cli-reference.md` (~L306-330, execute section): - One reusable agent session; first turn carries shared context + ordered queue; later tasks are compact continuations; UltraPlan checkpoints each task before advancing; stops on failure/cancellation; writes `.run-state.json` and `execute.md`; requires runtime evidence or a safe diagnostic before marking complete; constrains work to the project-index target; falls back to complete independent prompts when no reusable session ID is supplied. - Deferral: `--task --defer --reason ""` is durable and terminal, shown in execute.md and status counts; plan checkbox remains unchecked; review accepts deferrals only with a matching governed deferred outcome; arbitrary unchecked/manually checked tasks cannot bypass execution; `[/]` marker without `— Deferred: ` is invalid. # Context Pack: `sprint-execute-resume` — Sprint execute queue and resume

Target: ultraplan-go @ 8eef70f4903b25580719960009a170945bdad9ad (frozen, clean tree).
Planning context: ultraplan-workspace @ ab12dc38059c9bf485f9aced9075bcd7d924cac5.
Domain: governed-sprint-delivery. Risk: high. Descriptive only — no defect judgments.

## 1. Purpose

Executes the top-level task checkboxes of a validated `plan.md` through a reusable agent session, with product-owned durability around every agent turn:

- **Queue execution**: one ordered pass over plan tasks; first turn gets shared sprint context + full queue; later turns are compact continuations in the same session when a reusable session ID exists (fallback: independent full prompts).
- **Persist-before-launch checkpointing**: each task is persisted as `running` before the runtime call, and its terminal outcome is persisted before the next task starts; session IDs observed mid-stream are also checkpointed.
- **Stop-on-failure discipline**: queue halts on the first failed or cancelled task.
- **Stale-running reconcile**: `running` records left by dead owners become `failed` with diagnostics at three distinct points (startup recovery, resume reconciliation, pre-execution check).
- **Deferral protocol**: CLI `--defer --reason` (operator) or an agent-authored plan marker `- [/] Task N: ... — Deferred: <reason>` (agent); both require rationale and produce durable `deferred` outcomes; the plan checkbox stays visibly unchecked.
- **Resume validation**: `--resume` allows checked/deferred plan markers only when the run state already records matching terminal outcomes per stable task ID.
- **Containment**: the agent's working directory is set to the resolved approved target (worktree preferred), with in-prompt safety constraints forbidding git mutation and out-of-scope artifacts.
- **Publication**: when every task resolves (complete|deferred), git publication commits the implementation worktree (`All=true`) then the workspace artifacts (`execute.md`, `.run-state.json`), config-gated.

Primary code: `internal/sprint/execute.go`, `execute_plan.go`, `execute_state.go`, `execute_target.go`, `execute_model.go`, plus `internal/sprint/publication.go:57-78` and `internal/app/git_publication.go`.

The in-flight runtime call receives the same ctx. 129: - **Crash/restart**: orphaned `running` records recover to failed on startup reconcile or next resume; cleanup-uncertain marker forces explicit operator handling instead of silent reconcile (locks.go:40-44,101-108); legacy terminal states remain readable. 130: - **Retry**: rerunning without `--resume` rebuilds fresh state (prior file replaced on first save); failed/cancelled/pending tasks restart with Attempts++; `--resume` keeps complete/deferred history and continues the remaining queue, reusing the session when target and model still match. 131: - **Partial failure**: mixed-status state persisted, execute.md reflects counts, command exits ExitPartial-class with "execute completed with failed tasks". 132: - Publication failure after full resolution surfaces as command error while leaving all tasks resolved and state saved (commit may exist without push; push timeout bounded). 133: 134: ## 8. Immediate surface dependencies 135: 136: - **sprint-planning-chain**: `resolveSprintInputs`, `planManifest`, `ValidatePlanContent`, plan artifact reads, direct-input packet composition, shared prompt prefix/context pack. 137: - **sprint-flow-state**: flow dispatches execute (always Resume:true), skips its own publish step for execute, gates skip-checks via `ExecuteComplete`; execute itself does not write flow-state.json. 138: - **opencode-agent-runtime** (`internal/platform/runtime`): Request/Result/Event contract — SessionID/SessionAction continuation, OnEvent stream, Artifacts/Warnings driving completion classification, RuntimeStore scoping/cleanup, usage/metrics summaries. 139: - **repo-publication** (`internal/platform/gitpublish`): policy modes, repo lock, temp-index commit strategy, push semantics. 140: - **product-state-mirror** (`internal/productstate`): authoritative DB record {header, items keyed by task ID with ordinals} behind `ExecuteStateInDatabase`. 141: - **run-control / durable operations**: acceptance, claim, fencing, heartbeats, cancellation watch, terminal proposals wrapping every non-dry-run CLI execute. 142: - **workspace scaffold**: embedded `prompts/execute-sprint.md` documents the superseded agent-authored execution mode (writes legacy schemaVersion-0-style `.run-state.json` itself); still materialisable via `defaults install`. 143: 144: ## 9. Contracts (CURRENT-CONTRACT evidence) 145: 146: From target-repo `docs/cli-reference.md` (~L306-330, execute section): 147: - One reusable agent session; first turn carries shared context + ordered queue; later tasks are compact continuations; UltraPlan checkpoints each task before advancing; stops on failure/cancellation; writes `.run-state.json` and `execute.md`; requires runtime evidence or a safe diagnostic before marking complete; constrains work to the project-index target; falls back to complete independent prompts when no reusable session ID is supplied. 148: - Deferral: `--task --defer --reason ""` is durable and terminal, shown in execute.md and status counts; plan checkbox remains unchecked; review accepts deferrals only with a matching governed deferred outcome; arbitrary unchecked/manually checked tasks cannot bypass execution; `[/]` marker without `— Deferred: ` is invalid. 149: 150: From ultraplan-workspace sprint 23 (`projects/ultraplan-go/sprints/23-execute-stage/requirements.md` ~L22-49, L104): 151: - Versioned, atomic, strictly-loaded, resumable `.run-state.json` recording statuses with attempts, timestamps, diagnostics, runtime metadata summaries; stale running tasks recovered to retryable-or-failed with diagnostics without redoing complete tasks; sprint status reflects execute readiness without runtime calls; execute.md cites plan.md and records counts/evidence/diagnostics; same-directory atomic writes; malformed/unsupported schemas rejected with actionable diagnostics. 152: - Neutral divergence fact: sprint-23 enumerates five statuses (pending/running/complete/failed/cancelled); the implementation adds `deferred` as a sixth, documented instead in cli-reference.md. 153: 154: From ultraplan-workspace PRD (~L223, L576, L605): controlled execution from validated plan.md tasks is in scope; automatic Git-mutation *commands* and issue tracking remain deferred product non-goals (config-gated publication of completed work is implemented separately from the agent-side git ban). 155: 156: In-prompt contract (`ExecuteSafetyInstructions` + RenderExecutePrompt tail, execute.go:471-477): verifiable evidence or explicit safe diagnostic required; `[/]` + `— Deferred: ` protocol; never mark deferred work complete. 157: 158: HISTORY (context only): scaffold prompt `prompts/execute-sprint.md` describes agents writing their own legacy-shape `.run-state.json`; retained for materialisation compatibility and read back only by `LegacyTerminal*`/verify legacy paths. 159: 160: ## 10. Tests (evidence map) 161: 162: `internal/sprint`: 163: - `execute_plan_test.go`: happy-path extraction (traceability refs, evidence heuristics); deterministic stable IDs across whitespace normalization and re-id on identity change; rejection matrix (unsupported syntax, floating nested item, duplicate IDs, all-checked plan); resume-mode keeps checked parents; `[/]` requires reason and preserves stable ID; model annotation parses, stays out of the name, preserves ID; `executeSelectionForTask` annotation precedence; `ValidateExecute` end-to-end validity incl. rejecting fully-checked plans. 164: - `execute_state_test.go`: strict load/save round-trip; atomic write preserves prior file when rename hook blocks; 12-case validation failure table (schema, mismatch, unsafe paths, missing fields/timestamps, unsafe diagnostic/evidence, duplicate IDs, negative attempts); ErrMissing/ErrMalformed classification; legacy terminal state loads as historical only; deferred-without-rationale invalid and not counted failed; `DeferExecuteTask` persists rationale + summary; running-persist failure prevents any runtime call; session-checkpoint persist failure yields failed/state-save-failed task plus command error. 165: - `execute_target_test.go`: absolute + workspace-relative target resolution; missing/unavailable targets; `ValidateExecuteWorkdir` containment matrix (inside ok, outside/relative rejected); safety-instruction content. 166: - `execute_model_test.go`: full selection precedence chain including no-model error. 167: - `efficiency_improvements_test.go`: TestExecuteUsesOneSessionWithCompactPerTaskContinuations (two tasks → two requests; request 1 initial w/ queue size 2 and shared context; request 2 continue on recorded session with compact prompt; both tasks retain the shared session); TestExecuteFallsBackToFullPromptsWithoutReusableRuntimeSession (fresh-fallback full prompts); TestExecuteStopsSharedQueueAfterTaskFailure (one runtime call; task 2 stays pending; command errors). 168: - `publication_test.go`: TestPublishExecuteUsesTargetBeforeWorkspace (target-root All=true request precedes workspace paths request). 169: - `locks_test.go` (reconcile path): malformed run-state surfaces ErrExecuteRunStateMalformed. 170: - `prompt_context_test.go`, `efficiency_metrics_test.go`: PromptExecute composition, handbook injection, cache-directive metadata. 171: 172: Test-topology facts (neutral, for reviewer prioritization): the `--resume` branch internals — `reconcileExecuteState`, `validateResolvedResumeTasks`, `reusableExecuteSession`, the target-changed reuse guard (execute.go:186), and stale-running-on-resume — have no direct test hits (`Resume: true` appears only in production flow.go and app wiring; no sprint-package test constructs a resume run). `ValidateExecuteWorkdir` is unit-tested but no production caller was found; containment at the runtime boundary currently comes from direct assignment `runtimeReq.WorkDir = target.Path` (execute.go:245). Baseline `go test ./...` green at frozen commit. 173: 174: ## 11. Explicit unknowns / open questions 175: 176: 1. Intended enforcement point for workdir containment: `ValidateExecuteWorkdir` exists and is tested but unused in production; whether construction-by-assignment (`WorkDir = target.Path`) is the deliberate sole mechanism is undocumented. 177: 2. OpenCode adapter semantics for `SessionAction="continue"` and cross-process session reuse (whether a recorded SessionID remains continuable after process exit; whether OnEvent-reported SessionIDs can differ from the final Result.SessionID) — owned by the opencode-agent-runtime surface. 178: 3. productstate enablement conditions and migration timing (when `.run-state.json` flips from primary to mirror-once-terminal) — owned by product-state-mirror surface. 179: 4. Whether the single PlanFingerprint captured at state creation is meant to detect plan drift during long multi-task runs (it is not re-checked before publication); the deferral read-back revalidates structure per turn, but fingerprint staleness semantics are unspecified. 180: 5. Windows support depth: atomic rename/fsync/dir-sync assumptions in `saveExecuteRunStateWithHooks` and lock behavior appear POSIX-oriented; no platform-specific tests found. 182: 7. Whether the agent-authored legacy execution mode (scaffold prompt writing its own `.run-state.json`) is still a supported workflow or purely historical compatibility. 183: 8. Push credential expectations for `commit-and-push` (auth assumed pre-configured; interactive prompting disabled) and behavior when upstream ref configuration is inconsistent. 137: 	}
138: 	sp, tasks, target, selection, findings, err := s.prepareExecute(projectRef, sprintRef, req)
139: 	if err != nil {
140: 		return ExecuteResult{}, err
141: 	}
142: 	result := ExecuteResult{Project: sp.Project, Sprint: sp.Slug, DryRun: req.DryRun, Findings: findings}
143: 	if len(findings) > 0 {
144: 		return result, fmt.Errorf("execute prerequisites failed validation")
145: 	}
146: 	inputs, err := s.store.ReadPlanningInputs(sp)
147: 	if err != nil {
148: 		return result, err
149: 	}
150: 	sharedPrefix, err := s.prepareSharedPromptContext(ctx, sp, inputs, true)
151: 	if err != nil {
152: 		return result, err
153: 	}
154: 	if req.DryRun {
155: 		promptTask := tasks[0]
156: 		if req.TaskID != "" {
157: 			for _, task := range tasks {
158: 				if task.ID == req.TaskID {
159: 					promptTask = task
160: 					break
161: 				}
162: 			}
163: 		}
164: 		result.Prompt, err = composeStagePromptChecked(sharedPrefix, s.renderExecuteSessionPrompt(sp, promptTask, filterExecuteQueue(tasks, req.TaskID), target, executeSelectionForTask(selection, promptTask)))
165: 		if err != nil {
166: 			return result, err
167: 		}
168: 		result.Message = "execute dry run"
169: 		return result, nil
170: 	}
171: 	if s.runtime == nil {
172: 		return result, fmt.Errorf("runtime is required for execute")
173: 	}
174: 	now := s.now().UTC()
175: 	records := ExecuteTasksToRecords(tasks, func() time.Time { return now })
176: 	state := NewExecuteRunState(sp, target, ArtifactRelPath(sp, StagePlan), PlanFingerprint(mustReadPlan(s, sp)), records, now)
177: 	if existing, loadErr := LoadExecuteRunState(s.root, sp); loadErr == nil && req.Resume {
178: 		state = reconcileExecuteState(existing, records, now)
179: 	}
180: 	if err := SaveExecuteRunState(s.root, sp, state); err != nil {
181: 		return result, err
182: 	}
183: 	executionQueue := executeQueueFromState(state.Tasks, tasks, req.TaskID)
184: 	batchSessionID := ""
185: 	batchSessionModel := selection.Model
186: 	if req.Resume && filepath.Clean(state.Target.Path) == filepath.Clean(target.Path) {
187: 		if len(executionQueue) > 0 {
188: 			if first := taskByID(tasks, executionQueue[0].ID); first.ID != "" {
189: 				batchSessionModel = executeSelectionForTask(selection, first).Model
190: 			}
191: 		}
192: 		batchSessionID = reusableExecuteSession(state.Tasks, req.TaskID, batchSessionModel)
193: 	}
194: 	executionTurn := 0
195: 	for i := range state.Tasks {
196: 		task := &state.Tasks[i]
197: 		if req.TaskID != "" && task.ID != req.TaskID {
198: 			continue
199: 		}
200: 		if task.Status == ExecuteTaskComplete {
201: 			continue
202: 		}
203: 		if task.Status == ExecuteTaskRunning {
204: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskFailed
205: 			task.CompletedAt = ptrTime(now)
206: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "stale-running", Message: "recovered stale running task before resume", At: now})
207: 		}
208: 		if task.Status != ExecuteTaskPending && task.Status != ExecuteTaskFailed && task.Status != ExecuteTaskCancelled {
209: 			continue
210: 		}
211: 		start := s.now().UTC()
212: 		task.Status = ExecuteTaskRunning
213: 		task.Attempts++
214: 		task.StartedAt = &start
215: 		task.UpdatedAt = start
216: 		if err := SaveExecuteRunState(s.root, sp, state); err != nil {
217: 			return result, fmt.Errorf("persist running execute task %q: %w", task.ID, err)
218: 		}
219: 		planTask := taskByID(tasks, task.ID)
220: 		taskSelection := executeSelectionForTask(selection, planTask)
221: 		executionTurn++
222: 		continueSession := batchSessionID != "" && batchSessionModel == taskSelection.Model
223: 		stagePrompt := ""
224: 		promptPrefix := sharedPrefix
225: 		if continueSession {
226: 			stagePrompt = RenderExecuteContinuationPrompt(sp, planTask)
227: 			promptPrefix = ""
228: 		} else {
229: 			stagePrompt = s.renderExecuteSessionPrompt(sp, planTask, executionQueue, target, taskSelection)
230: 		}
231: 		composedPrompt, composeErr := composeStagePromptChecked(promptPrefix, stagePrompt)
232: 		if composeErr != nil {
233: 			return result, composeErr
234: 		}
235: 		sessionMode := "initial"
236: 		if continueSession {
237: 			sessionMode = "continue"
238: 		} else if executionTurn > 1 {
239: 			sessionMode = "fresh-fallback"
240: 		}
241: 		runtimeReq := s.runtimeRequest(composedPrompt, map[string]string{
242: 			"project": sp.Project, "sprint": sp.Slug, "stage": string(StageExecute), "task": task.ID, "model_source": taskSelection.Source,
243: 			"execution_session_mode": sessionMode, "execution_turn": fmt.Sprintf("%d", executionTurn), "execution_queue_size": fmt.Sprintf("%d", len(executionQueue)),
244: 		})
245: 		runtimeReq.WorkDir = target.Path
246: 		if continueSession {
247: 			runtimeReq.SessionID = batchSessionID
248: 			runtimeReq.SessionAction = "continue"
249: 		}
250: 		previousOnEvent := runtimeReq.OnEvent
251: 		var sessionMu sync.Mutex
252: 		var sessionSaveErr error
253: 		runtimeReq.OnEvent = func(event pruntime.Event) {
254: 			if previousOnEvent != nil {
255: 				previousOnEvent(event)
256: 			}
257: 			sessionMu.Lock()
258: 			defer sessionMu.Unlock()
259: 			if event.SessionID == "" || (task.Runtime != nil && task.Runtime.SessionID == event.SessionID) {
260: 				return
261: 			}
262: 			task.Runtime = &ExecuteRuntimeSummary{SessionID: event.SessionID, Model: taskSelection.Model, ModelSource: taskSelection.Source, OmissionReason: "raw runtime payloads omitted"}
263: 			task.UpdatedAt = s.now().UTC()
264: 			state.UpdatedAt = task.UpdatedAt
265: 			if err := SaveExecuteRunState(s.root, sp, state); err != nil && sessionSaveErr == nil {
266: 				sessionSaveErr = err
267: 			}
268: 		}
269: 		run, runErr := s.startSprintRuntime(ctx, sp, StageExecute, runtimeReq)
270: 		sessionMu.Lock()
271: 		checkpointErr := sessionSaveErr
272: 		sessionMu.Unlock()
273: 		result.Runtime = append(result.Runtime, run)
274: 		finish := s.now().UTC()
275: 		task.Runtime = mergeRuntimeSummary(task.Runtime, runtimeSummary(run, taskSelection))
276: 		if runErr == nil {
277: 			batchSessionID = run.SessionID
278: 			batchSessionModel = taskSelection.Model
279: 			if batchSessionID == "" && task.Runtime != nil {
280: 				batchSessionID = task.Runtime.SessionID
281: 			}
282: 		}
283: 		task.UpdatedAt = finish
284: 		task.CompletedAt = &finish
285: 		deferReason, deferErr := s.agentDeferredTaskReason(sp, task.ID)
286: 		switch {
287: 		case checkpointErr != nil:
288: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskFailed
289: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "state-save-failed", Message: safeExecuteText("execute.state_save_error", checkpointErr.Error()), At: finish})
290: 		case deferErr != nil:
291: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskFailed
292: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "invalid-deferral", Message: safeExecuteText("execute.defer_error", deferErr.Error()), At: finish})
293: 		case deferReason != "":
294: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskDeferred
295: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "deferred", Message: safeExecuteText("execute.defer_reason", deferReason), At: finish})
296: 		case ctx.Err() != nil:
297: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskCancelled
298: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "cancelled", Message: safeExecuteText("execute.cancelled", ctx.Err().Error()), At: finish})
299: 		case runErr != nil:
300: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskFailed
301: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "runtime-failed", Message: safeExecuteText("execute.runtime_error", safeError(runErr)), At: finish})
302: 		case len(run.Artifacts) > 0:
303: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskComplete
304: 			for _, artifact := range run.Artifacts {
305: 				task.Evidence = append(task.Evidence, ExecuteEvidence{Kind: artifact.Kind, Summary: safeExecuteText("execute.evidence", firstNonEmptyString(artifact.Description, artifact.ID)), Path: safeArtifactPath(artifact.URI)})
306: 			}
307: 		case hasDiagnosticOnlyCompletion(run):
308: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskComplete
309: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "diagnostic-only-completion", Message: "runtime reported safe diagnostic-only completion", At: finish})
310: 		default:
311: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskFailed
312: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "missing-evidence", Message: "runtime succeeded without expected evidence", At: finish})
313: 		}
314: 		if err := SaveExecuteRunState(s.root, sp, state); err != nil {
315: 			return result, fmt.Errorf("persist terminal execute task %q: %w", task.ID, err)
316: 		}
317: 		if checkpointErr != nil {
318: 			return result, fmt.Errorf("persist runtime session for execute task %q: %w", task.ID, checkpointErr)
319: 		}
320: 		if task.Status == ExecuteTaskFailed || task.Status == ExecuteTaskCancelled {
321: 			break
322: 		}
323: 		if req.TaskID != "" {
324: 			break
325: 		}
326: 	}
327: 	if err := WriteExecuteSummary(s.root, sp, state); err != nil {
328: 		return result, err
329: 	}
330: 	statePath, _ := ExecuteRunStatePath(s.root, sp)
331: 	result.RunStatePath = workspace.Rel(s.root, statePath)
332: 	result.SummaryPath = ArtifactRelPath(sp, StageExecute)
333: 	result.Tasks = state.Tasks
334: 	result.Message = executeResultMessage(state.Tasks)
335: 	if hasFailedExecuteTask(state.Tasks) {
336: 		return result, fmt.Errorf("execute completed with failed tasks")
337: 	}
338: 	for _, run := range result.Runtime {
339: 		_ = s.deleteCompletedSessions(ctx, run)
340: 	}
341: 	if allExecuteTasksResolved(state.Tasks) {
342: 		publications, publishErr := s.publishExecuteStage(ctx, sp, target)
343: 		result.Publications = append(result.Publications, publications...)
344: 		if publishErr != nil {
345: 			return result, publishErr
346: 		}
347: 	}
348: 	return result, nil
349: }

351: func (s Service) prepareExecute(projectRef, sprintRef string, req ExecuteRequest) (Sprint, []ExecutePlanTask, ExecuteTargetRef, ExecuteModelSelection, []ValidationFinding, error) {
352: 	sp, inputs, catalog, err := s.resolveSprintInputs(projectRef, sprintRef)
353: 	if err != nil {
354: 		return Sprint{}, nil, ExecuteTargetRef{}, ExecuteModelSelection{}, nil, err
355: 	}
356: 	manifest, findings := s.planManifest(sp, inputs, catalog)
357: 	var target ExecuteTargetRef
358: 	if len(findings) == 0 {
359: 		var targetFindings []ValidationFinding
360: 		target, targetFindings = s.resolveSprintTarget(sp, inputs.ProjectIndex, false)
361: 		findings = append(findings, targetFindings...)
362: 	}
363: 	var tasks []ExecutePlanTask
364: 	if len(findings) == 0 {
365: 		data, readErr := s.store.ReadArtifact(sp, StagePlan)
366: 		if readErr != nil {
367: 			findings = append(findings, finding("plan.md", "", ArtifactRelPath(sp, StagePlan), "missing plan", readErr.Error(), "Generate and validate plan.md before execute."))
368: 		} else {
369: 			tasks, findings = extractExecutePlanTasks(data, manifest, req.Resume)
370: 			if req.Resume && len(findings) == 0 {
371: 				findings = append(findings, s.validateResolvedResumeTasks(sp, tasks, manifest.OutputPath)...)
372: 			}
373: 		}
374: 	}
375: 	if req.TaskID != "" && len(findings) == 0 && taskByID(tasks, req.TaskID).ID == "" {
376: 		findings = append(findings, finding("Tasks", req.TaskID, ArtifactRelPath(sp, StagePlan), "unknown execute task", "selected task id does not exist in plan.md", "Use a task id from validate execute or run without --task."))
377: 	}
378: 	selection := s.executeModelSelection(req.ModelOverride)
379: 	if selection.Model == "" {
380: 		findings = append(findings, finding("Configuration", "execute model", "", "missing execute model", "no execute model configured", "Set planning.execute_model, planning.plan_model, models.primary, or models.default."))
381: 	}
382: 	sortSprintFindings(findings)
383: 	return sp, tasks, target, selection, findings, nil
384: }

386: func (s Service) validateResolvedResumeTasks(sp Sprint, tasks []ExecutePlanTask, planPath string) []ValidationFinding {
387: 	var resolved []ExecutePlanTask
388: 	for _, task := range tasks {
389: 		if task.Checked || task.Deferred {
390: 			resolved = append(resolved, task)
391: 		}
392: 	}
393: 	if len(resolved) == 0 {
394: 		return nil
395: 	}
396: 	state, err := LoadExecuteRunState(s.root, sp)
397: 	if err != nil {
398: 		return []ValidationFinding{finding("Tasks", "", planPath, "checked tasks lack execution state", "one or more top-level tasks are checked but no valid resumable execution state exists", "Restore the matching .run-state.json or leave tasks unchecked for a new execution.")}
399: 	}
400: 	byID := make(map[string]ExecuteTaskStatus, len(state.Tasks))
401: 	for _, task := range state.Tasks {
402: 		byID[task.ID] = task.Status
403: 	}
404: 	var findings []ValidationFinding
405: 	for _, task := range resolved {
406: 		expected := ExecuteTaskComplete
407: 		problem := "checked task is not complete in execution state"
408: 		detail := "top-level task is checked without a matching complete run-state record"
409: 		suggestion := "Restore the task checkbox to unchecked or reconcile the execution state before resuming."
410: 		if task.Deferred {
411: 			expected = ExecuteTaskDeferred
412: 			problem = "plan deferral is not recorded in execution state"
413: 			detail = "top-level task uses [/] without a matching deferred run-state record"
414: 			suggestion = "Resume the owning execute attempt so it can record the deferral, or restore the task marker to unchecked."
415: 		}
416: 		if byID[task.ID] != expected {
417: 			findings = append(findings, finding("Tasks", task.Name, planPath, problem, detail, suggestion))
418: 		}
419: 	}
420: 	return findings
421: }

423: func (s Service) agentDeferredTaskReason(sp Sprint, taskID string) (string, error) {
424: 	data, err := s.store.ReadArtifact(sp, StagePlan)
425: 	if err != nil {
426: 		return "", err
427: 	}
428: 	inputs, err := s.store.ReadPlanningInputs(sp)
429: 	if err != nil {
430: 		return "", err
431: 	}
432: 	catalog, parseFindings := project.ParseProjectIndex(inputs.ProjectIndex)
433: 	if len(parseFindings) > 0 {
434: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("project-index.md has malformed catalog rows")
435: 	}
436: 	manifest, findings := s.planManifest(sp, inputs, catalog)
437: 	if len(findings) > 0 {
438: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("plan manifest is invalid")
439: 	}
440: 	tasks, findings := extractExecutePlanTasks(data, manifest, true)
441: 	if len(findings) > 0 {
442: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("plan changed to an invalid task state")
443: 	}
444: 	for _, task := range tasks {
445: 		if task.ID == taskID && task.Deferred {
446: 			return task.DeferReason, nil
447: 		}
448: 	}
449: 	return "", nil
450: }

519: func renderExecuteQueue(currentTaskID string, queue []ExecutePlanTask) string {
520: 	if len(queue) == 0 {
521: 		return ""
522: 	}
523: 	var b strings.Builder
524: 	b.WriteString("\n## Ordered Sprint Execution Queue\n\n")
525: 	b.WriteString("This agent session owns the complete ordered queue below. Execute only the current task during this turn; UltraPlan will checkpoint its evidence before advancing the same session.\n\n")
526: 	for index, task := range queue {
527: 		marker := "queued"
528: 		if task.ID == currentTaskID {
529: 			marker = "current"
530: 		}
531: 		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%d. [%s] `%s` — %s\n", index+1, marker, task.ID, task.Name)
532: 	}
533: 	return b.String()
534: }

536: func filterExecuteQueue(tasks []ExecutePlanTask, taskID string) []ExecutePlanTask {
537: 	if taskID == "" {
538: 		return append([]ExecutePlanTask(nil), tasks...)
539: 	}
540: 	selected := taskByID(tasks, taskID)
541: 	if selected.ID == "" {
542: 		return nil
543: 	}
544: 	return []ExecutePlanTask{selected}

547: func executeQueueFromState(records []ExecuteTaskRecord, tasks []ExecutePlanTask, taskID string) []ExecutePlanTask {
548: 	queue := make([]ExecutePlanTask, 0, len(records))
549: 	for _, record := range records {
550: 		if taskID != "" && record.ID != taskID {
551: 			continue
552: 		}
553: 		if record.Status == ExecuteTaskComplete || record.Status == ExecuteTaskDeferred {
554: 			continue
555: 		}
556: 		if task := taskByID(tasks, record.ID); task.ID != "" {
557: 			queue = append(queue, task)
558: 		}
559: 	}
560: 	return queue
561: }

563: func reusableExecuteSession(records []ExecuteTaskRecord, taskID, model string) string {
564: 	sessionID := ""
565: 	for _, record := range records {
566: 		if taskID != "" && record.ID != taskID {
567: 			continue
568: 		}
569: 		if record.Runtime != nil && record.Runtime.Model == model && record.Runtime.SessionID != "" {
570: 			sessionID = record.Runtime.SessionID
571: 		}
572: 	}
573: 	return sessionID
574: }

576: func WriteExecuteSummary(root string, sp Sprint, state ExecuteRunState) error {
577: 	path, err := resolveSprintContained(root, sp, ArtifactRelPath(sp, StageExecute))
578: 	if err != nil {
579: 		return err
580: 	}
581: 	var b strings.Builder
582: 	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "# Execute Summary\n\nPlan: `%s`\nRun state: `%s`\n\n", state.PlanPath, ExecuteRunStateRelPath(sp))
583: 	counts := map[ExecuteTaskStatus]int{}
584: 	for _, task := range state.Tasks {
585: 		counts[task.Status]++
586: 	}
587: 	fmt.Fprintln(&b, "## Task Counts")
588: 	fmt.Fprintln(&b)
589: 	for _, status := range ExecuteTaskStatuses() {
590: 		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- %s: %d\n", status, counts[status])
591: 	}
592: 	fmt.Fprintln(&b, "\n## Tasks")
593: 	fmt.Fprintln(&b)
594: 	for _, task := range state.Tasks {
595: 		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- `%s` %s: %s (attempts: %d)\n", task.ID, task.Status, task.Identity.Name, task.Attempts)
596: 		for _, evidence := range task.Evidence {
597: 			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  - evidence: %s %s\n", evidence.Kind, evidence.Summary)
598: 		}
599: 		for _, diagnostic := range task.Diagnostics {
600: 			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  - diagnostic: %s %s\n", diagnostic.Code, diagnostic.Message)
601: 		}
602: 	}
603: 	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
604: 		return err
605: 	}
606: 	return os.WriteFile(path, []byte(b.String()), 0o644)
607: }

reasoning_details.text:
Interesting things in execute_state.go:

1. `safeRelPath` — checks `clean != "."` and no "../" prefix. What about a path like "foo/../../bar"? filepath.Clean would normalize to "../bar" → caught. What about Windows-style backslash? On linux, backslash is a normal char. OK.

2. `ValidateExecuteRunState` — deferred requires completedAt + rationale. Terminal requires completedAt. Running requires StartedAt. But **pending tasks don't require anything beyond basics** — fine.

3. Note: `saveExecuteRunStateWithHooks` sets `state.UpdatedAt = time.Now().UTC()` — mutates the copy (value receiver) — fine.

4. **DB-mirror mode**: when authoritative, save writes DB then file only at checkpoint. Load prefers DB. In Execute's flow: `SaveExecuteRunState` after marking running — in DB mode, file NOT updated until all terminal. If crash mid-run with DB enabled, resume loads from DB. OK.

But wait — subtle issue: in DB-authoritative mode, `LoadExecuteRunState` prefers DB; if DB record not found (`found=false`), falls to file. Migration timing unknown #3.

5. `LegacyTerminalExecuteStatus` reads raw file even when DB authoritative — legacy shape has schemaVersion 0, DB wouldn't have it. Fine.

Now — one potentially significant correctness issue: **`LoadExecuteRunState` returns error wrapping ErrExecuteRunStateMissing when file absent. In Execute line 177**: `if existing, loadErr := LoadExecuteRunState(s.root, sp); loadErr == nil && req.Resume { state = reconcileExecuteState(...) }`. So on resume with missing/corrupt state → fresh silently. The context pack flags this as neutral note. With validateResolvedResumeTasks guarding checked markers... but if plan unchecked and state corrupt → fresh run re-executes everything including completed work. Is that a defect? It re-does work but doesn't produce wrong records per se. The prior state file gets overwritten on first save. Data loss of history. Hmm — "resume validation against plan markers" contract: resume allows checked/deferred markers only when matching terminal outcomes exist. Unchecked + corrupt state → fresh execution. That seems like intended fallback ("Restore ... or leave tasks unchecked for a new execution"). Not a strong defect.

6. Now think about `reconcileExecuteState` + stale-running → failed. On resume, a running task becomes failed BEFORE being retried, then the loop hits it: status failed → proceeds to retry. Good.

But NOTE: reconcile happens ONLY on resume. Non-resume fresh run: `state = NewExecuteRunState(...)` fresh — discards old state entirely. Startup reconcile (`ReconcileInterruptedMutation`) handles dead-owner running records. Need to check locks.go for that.

7. Another thing: `ValidateExecuteRunState` requires `state.Target.Path != ""` and Source non-empty. NewExecuteRunState stores target ref. On reconcile, existing header kept (existing.Tasks replaced). So Target stays OLD target path. Session reuse guard compares state.Target.Path vs current target.Path — mismatch → no reuse. Good.

Now execute_target.go and execute_model.go.

29: func ResolveExecuteTarget(workspaceRoot, projectIndexContent string) (ExecuteTargetRef, []ValidationFinding) {

33: 	}
34: 	clean := filepath.Clean(target)
35: 	if !filepath.IsAbs(clean) {
36: 		if strings.TrimSpace(workspaceRoot) == "" {
37: 			return ExecuteTargetRef{}, []ValidationFinding{finding("Project Scope", "Target Implementation Directory", target, "relative target has no workspace root", "the target cannot be resolved without the UltraPlan workspace root", "Run the command from a valid UltraPlan workspace or use an absolute target path.")}
38: 		}
39: 		clean = filepath.Join(workspaceRoot, clean)
40: 	}
41: 	resolved, err := filepath.Abs(clean)
42: 	if err != nil {
43: 		return ExecuteTargetRef{}, []ValidationFinding{finding("Project Scope", "Target Implementation Directory", target, "target path cannot be resolved", err.Error(), "Use a valid absolute path or a path relative to the UltraPlan workspace root.")}
44: 	}
45: 	clean = filepath.Clean(resolved)
46: 	info, err := os.Stat(clean)
47: 	if err != nil {
48: 		return ExecuteTargetRef{}, []ValidationFinding{finding("Project Scope", "Target Implementation Directory", target, "target root unavailable", err.Error(), "Create or restore the approved target repository before execute.")}
49: 	}
50: 	if !info.IsDir() {
51: 		return ExecuteTargetRef{}, []ValidationFinding{finding("Project Scope", "Target Implementation Directory", target, "target root is not a directory", "path exists but is not a directory", "Use the approved target repository directory.")}
52: 	}
53: 	return ExecuteTargetRef{Path: clean, Source: "project-index.md"}, nil

56: func (s Service) resolveSprintTarget(sp Sprint, projectIndex string, create bool) (ExecuteTargetRef, []ValidationFinding) {
57: 	if s.codeContextTarget != nil {
58: 		return s.codeContextTarget(projectIndex)
59: 	}
60: 	source, findings := ResolveExecuteTarget(s.root, projectIndex)
61: 	if len(findings) > 0 {
62: 		return ExecuteTargetRef{}, findings
63: 	}
64: 	record, err := loadSprintWorkspace(sp)
65: 	if err == nil {
66: 		if validateErr := validateSprintWorkspace(record, source.Path); validateErr != nil {
67: 			return ExecuteTargetRef{}, []ValidationFinding{finding("Sprint Workspace", "workspace", workspace.Rel(s.root, sprintWorkspacePath(sp)), "invalid sprint workspace", validateErr.Error(), "Restore the recorded worktree or explicitly recreate the sprint workspace.")}
68: 		}
69: 		return ExecuteTargetRef{Path: record.Path, Source: ".workspace.json"}, nil
70: 	}
71: 	if !os.IsNotExist(err) {
72: 		return ExecuteTargetRef{}, []ValidationFinding{finding("Sprint Workspace", "workspace", workspace.Rel(s.root, sprintWorkspacePath(sp)), "unreadable sprint workspace", err.Error(), "Repair or remove the malformed sprint workspace record.")}
73: 	}
74: 	if !create {
75: 		return source, nil
76: 	}
77: 	record, err = createSprintWorkspace(sp, source.Path, s.now().UTC())
78: 	if err != nil {
79: 		return ExecuteTargetRef{}, []ValidationFinding{finding("Sprint Workspace", "workspace", source.Path, "cannot create sprint workspace", err.Error(), "Commit or stash source changes, remove any conflicting branch or worktree, then retry.")}
80: 	}
81: 	return ExecuteTargetRef{Path: record.Path, Source: ".workspace.json"}, nil

84: func loadSprintWorkspace(sp Sprint) (SprintWorkspace, error) {
85: 	data, err := os.ReadFile(sprintWorkspacePath(sp))
86: 	if err != nil {
87: 		return SprintWorkspace{}, err

91: 		return SprintWorkspace{}, fmt.Errorf("decode sprint workspace: %w", err)
92: 	}
93: 	if record.SchemaVersion != sprintWorkspaceSchemaVersion || record.SourceRoot == "" || record.Path == "" || record.Branch == "" || record.Baseline == "" {

99: func validateSprintWorkspace(record SprintWorkspace, source string) error {
100: 	if filepath.Clean(record.SourceRoot) != filepath.Clean(source) {
101: 		return fmt.Errorf("project target changed from %q to %q", record.SourceRoot, source)
102: 	}
103: 	info, err := os.Stat(record.Path)
104: 	if err != nil {
105: 		return fmt.Errorf("worktree unavailable: %w", err)
106: 	}
107: 	if !info.IsDir() {
108: 		return fmt.Errorf("worktree path is not a directory")
109: 	}
110: 	sourceCommon, err := gitCommonDirectory(source)
111: 	if err != nil {
112: 		return fmt.Errorf("source Git metadata unavailable: %w", err)
113: 	}
114: 	workspaceCommon, err := gitCommonDirectory(record.Path)
115: 	if err != nil || workspaceCommon != sourceCommon {
116: 		return fmt.Errorf("worktree belongs to a different Git repository")
117: 	}
118: 	branch, err := gitOutput(record.Path, "branch", "--show-current")
119: 	if err != nil || strings.TrimSpace(branch) != record.Branch {
120: 		return fmt.Errorf("worktree is not on recorded branch %q", record.Branch)
121: 	}
122: 	return nil

125: func gitCommonDirectory(dir string) (string, error) {
126: 	common, err := gitOutput(dir, "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir")
127: 	if err != nil {
128: 		return "", err
129: 	}
130: 	if !filepath.IsAbs(common) {
131: 		common = filepath.Join(dir, common)
132: 	}
133: 	return filepath.Abs(filepath.Clean(common))

136: func createSprintWorkspace(sp Sprint, source string, now time.Time) (SprintWorkspace, error) {
137: 	root, err := gitOutput(source, "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel")
138: 	if err != nil {
139: 		return SprintWorkspace{}, fmt.Errorf("target is not a Git worktree: %w", err)
140: 	}
141: 	root = filepath.Clean(root)
142: 	if filepath.Clean(source) != root {
143: 		return SprintWorkspace{}, fmt.Errorf("target must be the Git worktree root %q", root)
144: 	}
145: 	dirty, err := gitOutput(source, "status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=normal")
146: 	if err != nil {
147: 		return SprintWorkspace{}, fmt.Errorf("inspect target status: %w", err)
148: 	}
149: 	if strings.TrimSpace(dirty) != "" {
150: 		return SprintWorkspace{}, fmt.Errorf("target has uncommitted changes")
151: 	}
152: 	baseline, err := gitOutput(source, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
153: 	if err != nil {
154: 		return SprintWorkspace{}, fmt.Errorf("resolve target HEAD: %w", err)
155: 	}
156: 	branch := "ultraplan/" + safeGitComponent(sp.Project) + "/" + safeGitComponent(sp.Slug)
157: 	parent := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(root), "."+filepath.Base(root)+"-ultraplan-worktrees")
158: 	path := filepath.Join(parent, safeGitComponent(sp.Project), safeGitComponent(sp.Slug))
159: 	if _, err := os.Lstat(path); !os.IsNotExist(err) {
160: 		return SprintWorkspace{}, fmt.Errorf("worktree path already exists: %s", path)
161: 	}
162: 	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
163: 		return SprintWorkspace{}, fmt.Errorf("create worktree parent: %w", err)
164: 	}
165: 	cmd := exec.Command("git", "-C", source, "worktree", "add", "-b", branch, path, strings.TrimSpace(baseline))
166: 	if output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
167: 		return SprintWorkspace{}, fmt.Errorf("git worktree add: %s: %w", strings.TrimSpace(string(output)), err)
168: 	}
169: 	record := SprintWorkspace{SchemaVersion: sprintWorkspaceSchemaVersion, SourceRoot: root, Path: path, Branch: branch, Baseline: strings.TrimSpace(baseline), CreatedAt: now}
170: 	data, err := json.MarshalIndent(record, "", "  ")
171: 	if err != nil {
172: 		return SprintWorkspace{}, err
173: 	}
174: 	data = append(data, '\n')
175: 	if err := atomicWriteFile(sprintWorkspacePath(sp), data); err != nil {
176: 		_ = exec.Command("git", "-C", source, "worktree", "remove", path).Run()
177: 		_ = exec.Command("git", "-C", source, "branch", "-D", branch).Run()
178: 		return SprintWorkspace{}, fmt.Errorf("persist sprint workspace: %w", err)
179: 	}
180: 	return record, nil
181: }

reasoning_details.text:
Notes on execute_target.go:

1. `ResolveExecuteTarget` — extracts target from project-index.md. `filepath.Join(workspaceRoot, clean)` — if clean is like "../../etc", Join resolves... filepath.Join cleans the result, so "/ws/../../etc" → "/etc"? Actually Join("/ws", "../../etc") = Clean("/ws/../../etc") = "/etc". Yes — path traversal out of workspace root is permitted by design? The target dir is user/agent-controlled via project-index.md; pointing outside workspace root is allowed for absolute paths anyway (absolute targets allowed). So relative traversal adds nothing beyond absolute. Not a defect per doctrine (the operator approves project-index via planning chain validation presumably).

2. `validateSprintWorkspace` compares branch current == record.Branch. If worktree detached → branch empty ≠ record.Branch → invalid. OK.

3. `gitCommonDirectory`: if common dir relative, join with dir. For worktrees, `rev-parse --git-common-dir` returns absolute usually or relative like ".git". Fine.

4. `createSprintWorkspace` — rollback on record write failure removes worktree+branch. Note `_ = exec.Command("git", "-C", source, "worktree", "remove", path).Run()` — without --force; worktree has no changes (fresh at baseline) so fine.

5. **`extractTargetImplementationDirectory`** regex: first bold form `- **Target Implementation Directory:** value`. Note the colon inside bold. Second plain form `- Target Implementation Directory: value`. What about a heading form `**Target Implementation Directory:**` not as list item? Only list items matched. Fine.

Now execute_model.go and git_publication.go, plus locks.go for reconcile, publication.go, service.go runtimeRequest, flow.go wiring, verify.go requireCompleteExecute.

13: // The mutation lease is product-owned and shared by flow, execute, review,
14: // smoke, and verify. A context marker permits composite workflows to invoke
15: // child stages without reacquiring the same cross-process file lock.
16: type mutationLeaseContextKey struct{}
17: 
18: type mutationLeaseContext struct {
19: 	path string
20: }

22: // ReconcileInterruptedMutation converts durable running records left by a
23: // dead owner into explicit interrupted evidence. A live cross-process lease is
24: // never rewritten.
25: func (s Service) ReconcileInterruptedMutation(ctx context.Context, projectRef, sprintRef string) (bool, error) {
26: 	lockedCtx, release, err := s.acquireMutationContext(ctx, projectRef, sprintRef)
27: 	if err != nil {
28: 		if errors.Is(err, ErrVerificationConflict) {
29: 			return false, nil
30: 		}
31: 		return false, err
32: 	}
33: 	defer release()
34: 	_ = lockedCtx
35: 	sp, err := s.resolveMutationSprint(projectRef, sprintRef)
36: 	if err != nil {
37: 		return false, err
38: 	}
39: 	now := s.now().UTC()
40: 	_, uncertaintyErr := loadCleanupUncertain(sp)
41: 	hasUncertainty := uncertaintyErr == nil
42: 	if uncertaintyErr != nil && !errors.Is(uncertaintyErr, os.ErrNotExist) {
43: 		return false, uncertaintyErr
44: 	}
45: 	changed := false
46: 	state, err := LoadExecuteRunState(s.root, sp)
47: 	if err == nil {
48: 		for i := range state.Tasks {
49: 			if state.Tasks[i].Status != ExecuteTaskRunning {
50: 				continue
51: 			}
52: 			state.Tasks[i].Status = ExecuteTaskFailed
53: 			state.Tasks[i].UpdatedAt = now
54: 			state.Tasks[i].CompletedAt = &now
55: 			state.Tasks[i].Diagnostics = append(state.Tasks[i].Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "recovery-interrupted", Message: "running task belonged to a stopped process; inspect durable target state before resuming", At: now})
56: 			changed = true
57: 		}
58: 		if changed {
59: 			state.UpdatedAt = now
60: 			if err := SaveExecuteRunState(s.root, sp, state); err != nil {
61: 				return false, err
62: 			}
63: 		}
64: 	} else if !errors.Is(err, ErrExecuteRunStateMissing) && !legacyTerminalExecuteRunState(s.root, sp) {
65: 		return false, err
66: 	}
67: 	flow, flowErr := LoadFlowState(s.root, sp)
68: 	if flowErr == nil {
69: 		if reconcileExpiredAttempts(&flow, now) {
70: 			flow.UpdatedAt = now
71: 			if err := SaveFlowState(s.root, sp, flow); err != nil {
72: 				return false, err
73: 			}
74: 			changed = true
75: 		}
76: 		qaStore := NewQAStore(s.root, sp)
77: 		if qaPath, pathErr := qaStore.StatePath(); pathErr == nil {
78: 			if _, statErr := os.Lstat(qaPath); statErr == nil {
79: 				qaState, qaErr := qaStore.LoadState()
80: 				if qaErr != nil {
81: 					return false, qaErr
82: 				}
83: 				switch qaState.Phase {
84: 				case QAPhaseQueued, QAPhaseRunning, QAPhaseSynthesizing:
85: 					qaState.Phase = QAPhaseInterrupted
86: 					qaState.Run.Lifecycle = QARunTerminal
87: 					qaState.Run.TerminalResult = QATerminalInterrupted
88: 					qaState.Blocker = &QABlocker{Category: QAErrorConflict, Scope: "attempt", Summary: "the prior QA owner stopped before recording a terminal result", NextAction: "Run qa recover, then qa resume with a new durable owner."}
89: 					qaState.NextAction = qaState.Blocker.NextAction
90: 					qaState.UpdatedAt = now
91: 					if err := qaStore.SaveRecoveredState(qaState, flow); err != nil {
92: 						return false, err
93: 					}
94: 					changed = true
95: 				}
96: 			}
97: 		}
98: 	} else if !errors.Is(flowErr, ErrFlowStateMissing) && !legacyFlowState(s.root, sp) {
99: 		return false, flowErr
100: 	}

103: 			return false, err
104: 		}
105: 	}

108: 	}

112: func (s Service) acquireMutationContext(ctx context.Context, projectRef, sprintRef string) (context.Context, func(), error) {

114: 	if err != nil {

116: 	}

118: 	if held, ok := ctx.Value(mutationLeaseContextKey{}).(mutationLeaseContext); ok && held.path == path {
119: 		return ctx, func() {}, nil
120: 	}
121: 	release, err := s.acquireMutation(projectRef, sprintRef)
122: 	if err != nil {
123: 		return ctx, nil, err
124: 	}
125: 	return context.WithValue(ctx, mutationLeaseContextKey{}, mutationLeaseContext{path: path}), release, nil
126: }

138: 	if err != nil {
139: 		return Sprint{}, err
140: 	}

142: 	return sp, err
143: }

The tests never assert that the annotated model reaches `req.Model`. So the annotation → runtime selection gap stands as a candidate defect. But wait — I need to check whether there's a contract that says the annotation should select the model at runtime. The code comment in execute_plan.go says: "Model optionally overrides the runtime model (provider/model) for this task via an inline `<!-- model: provider/model -->` plan annotation." That's an in-code contract: "overrides the runtime model". And `executeSelectionForTask` doc comment: "resolves one task's effective model selection. An inline plan annotation wins over the batch selection".

And in execute.go, `taskSelection` is used for:
1. metadata model_source
2. continueSession comparison
3. prompt rendering ("Model source")
4. runtime summary Model/ModelSource recorded in state

But NOT for the actual request. The batch path: when no annotation, taskSelection = selection whose Model came from s.stageRuntime[StageExecute].Model etc. And runtimeRequest applies stage override to req.Provider/Model — consistent for the batch case. For annotated tasks, inconsistent.

Hmm wait — actually let me double-check: does `runtimeRequest`'s stage override use `s.runtimeForStage(stage)` which returns StageRuntime{Model, Variant}. In production wiring (`sprintRuntimeService`, app layer), stageRuntime[StageExecute].Model comes from config planning.execute_model. So req.Provider/req.Model = planning.execute_model. If a task has an annotation, the request STILL uses planning.execute_model.

So yes: the actual model used for an annotated task is the batch model, while everything recorded claims the annotated model was used. This is a real defect: misleading state records + wrong runtime behavior vs the in-code contract. Severity: medium-high (wrong outcome, misleading audit trail; also session-matching decisions made on phantom models). Confidence: high on mechanics. Let me verify there is truly no other place where Provider/Model gets overridden per task... Search in execute.go — no. Also check opencode adapter `requestVariantRuntime` — maybe variant wrapping reads metadata["variant"]? That's Variant only.

Let me quickly double check `runtimeRequest` once more (service.go 1122-1195): `req := s.runtimeConfig` — base config includes Provider/Model from models.primary/default. Then stage override replaces them if stageRuntime has the stage with non-empty model. No task-level input exists. Confirmed.

Now — is this maybe intentional "annotation only informs prompt"? The comment explicitly says "optionally overrides the runtime model (provider/model) for this task". So it's a bug against its own documented intent.

Next candidates to investigate:

1. OnEvent concurrency race: `task.Runtime` written under sessionMu inside wrapper but main goroutine writes `task.Runtime = mergeRuntimeSummary(task.Runtime, ...)` at line 275 without the mutex, and events may arrive concurrently? Depends on runtime adapter: are events emitted synchronously during StartRun (same goroutine) or async from event pump goroutine? Check internal/platform/runtime/runtime.go StartRun — likely pumps events from a channel via goroutine, possibly after StartRun returns? Need to check whether all events complete before Result returned. Let me look.

2. `reusableExecuteSession` + `batchSessionID` update on success even when run.SessionID empty and task.Runtime nil → batchSessionID="" → next task fresh-fallback. OK.

3. Defer CLI: `DeferExecuteTask` — allows deferring a RUNNING task (status running). It sets deferred without clearing StartedAt — validation OK. Fine.

4. Resume + TaskID: `validateResolvedResumeTasks` runs over ALL resolved markers even when --task narrows. Good.

5. **Fresh-run overwrite hazard**: Non-resume Execute unconditionally rebuilds state from plan and saves — wiping prior history including completed tasks. Then executionQueue excludes complete/deferred records... wait, in a FRESH run, all records start pending! `records := ExecuteTasksToRecords(tasks, now)` — every record pending regardless of previous completion or plan checkboxes... Important finding regarding the OnEvent race: In `Adapter.StartRun`, the event goroutine ranges over `run.Events()` and calls `req.OnEvent(mapped)` concurrently with the main flow. After `run.Wait` returns, StartRun waits up to 1 second for eventsCh. If events channel closes within 1s, all OnEvent calls have completed (the goroutine sends to eventsCh AFTER closing loop). But if it times out (`case <-time.After(time.Second)`), StartRun returns while the event goroutine may STILL be invoking `req.OnEvent` — meaning in execute.go, `task.Runtime = mergeRuntimeSummary(task.Runtime, ...)` (execute.go:275) and subsequent `SaveExecuteRunState` can race with the OnEvent closure writing `task.Runtime`/saving state.

The execute.go OnEvent wrapper guards its own saves with sessionMu, but the main-loop mutations at lines 275-284 (`task.Runtime=`, `task.UpdatedAt=`, `task.CompletedAt=`) are NOT under sessionMu; also line 314 terminal SaveExecuteRunState is not under sessionMu. So if OnEvent fires late (>1s after Wait), we get a concurrent map/state write → potential data race producing corrupted state or a panic (`concurrent map writes`? state.Tasks slice element mutation — data race on struct fields; JSON marshal of partially-mutated state).

How plausible: events stream typically closes promptly after run completion; but on cancellation path (`ctx.Done` + 5s timeout return at line 376), StartRun returns immediately while the event pump may still be running — OnEvent keeps firing during task classification and terminal persist! That's the cancellation path: ctx cancelled → mapped cancelled returned after 5s wait OR immediately at `<-time.After(5 * time.Second)` branch... Actually in that branch they return after 5s of no wait result. The events goroutine continues. Then execute.go classifies cancelled, persists terminal state while OnEvent concurrently saves state (with running status? no—OnEvent sets task.Runtime only, status stays whatever it was—running) and mutates task.UpdatedAt/state.UpdatedAt. Race on ExecuteRunState struct fields between goroutine and main. Also two concurrent SaveExecuteRunState calls → atomic rename each, last-writer-wins; could resurrect "running" status over "cancelled"? Sequence: main sets cancelled, saves; OnEvent (late event) sets task.Runtime, task.UpdatedAt=now, state.UpdatedAt, saves — writing task.Status as CURRENT value (cancelled since shared pointer)... Actually both share the same `state` object; the OnEvent save marshals current shared state — status would be cancelled by then. The race is memory-level unsynchronized access (Go data race, undefined behavior) plus interleaved file writes. It's real but timing-dependent.

Is this worth reporting? It's a genuine data race under the runtime adapter's documented timeout path (events not drained within 1s) or the cancellation fast-path. The sprint execute code explicitly added sessionMu to serialize checkpoint saves — showing intent to handle concurrency — yet main-loop writes bypass it. Execute does NOT. Neither the batch selection (from --model override or planning.execute_model) nor per-task annotations are applied to runtimeReq.Provider/Model. Wait — for the batch case WITHOUT annotation, does it matter? runtimeRequest applies stage override planning.execute_model → matches selection source "planning.execute_model". If selection came from "command override" (--model) or "planning.plan_model" or "runtime.config", then:
- command override: request uses stage override if configured else base config — NOT the override. So `sprint 1 2 execute --model vendor/x` runs on whatever config model. That's a second layer of the same defect: CLI --model is silently ignored for execute (while recorded as "command override" in state/prompt).
- planning.plan_model fallback: stageRuntime has StagePlan? planningStageRuntime(effective.Config) presumably maps planning.execute_model→StageExecute and planning.plan_model→StagePlan etc. Let me check planningStageRuntime.
